manifest.name: dsh-rea
manifest.description: Registers the upstream REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) MCP server into DeepSeek Harness as mcp__rea__* tools — a third-party adapter, analysis is upstream's. · 把上游 REA 的 MCP 服务接入 DeepSeek Harness，提供 mcp__rea__* 工具（第三方适配，分析能力属上游）。
manifest.author: tudamu

bundle.text:
# dsh-rea — REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) as native DSH tools
#
# One row: the dsh-rea host plugin. It mounts the official MCP client
# (@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client) for the upstream `rea --mcp` stdio server, so
# the model sees mcp__rea__<tool>, and owns the settings shown on this bundle's
# page in the Plugins sidebar:
#
#   ghidraInstallDir   Ghidra 12.1.x directory, passed as GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR
#   toolCallTimeoutMs  per-call timeout (default 300000)
#
# Both are volatile: saving them on the Plugins page restarts the REA child
# with the new values. To pin them by hand instead, override this row from
# your profile's own cordis.patch.yml:
#
#   - id: rea
#     config:
#       ghidraInstallDir: /Applications/ghidra_12.1.1_PUBLIC
#
# Prerequisite: `rea` 6.3.0 or newer on the PATH the harness sees
# (`npm i -g rea-agents@latest`). The command form is chosen per OS
# (Windows: cmd.exe /c rea --mcp; POSIX: rea --mcp). A missing REA never
# blocks harness startup.

- insert:
    - id: rea
      name: dsh-rea

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-rea)

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Brings the upstream **[REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea)** MCP server into
**DeepSeek Harness** (dsh), so its tools show up in a session as `mcp__rea__*`.

A small DSH bundle. Its one row, `rea`, mounts the official MCP client plugin
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`) for the `rea --mcp` stdio server already installed on your machine, and adds
a page to the **Plugins** sidebar with a setup check, example prompts, and settings. There is no analysis
code here.

> **Third-party adapter.** This repository is not part of REA, ships none of REA's code, and is not
> maintained by REA's authors. It connects REA and adds a setup page.
> Upstream: [github.com/morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea) (MIT) ·
> [docs](https://github.com/morluto/rea#what-you-can-analyze) ·
> [中文文档](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/README_zh.md#可以分析什么) ·
> [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/) · npm package `rea-agents`.
> REA's own problems go to its tracker; **this plugin's** problems go to
> [this repository's issues](https://github.com/dushudou/dsh-rea/issues).

**It adds:** the `mcp__rea__*` tool registration with cross-platform auto-detection of the command form,
and a Plugins-page guide that tells you what is missing and how to fix it.

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text: The analysis is upstream's; this section only restates upstream's own contract so expectations are right.

readme.section: What it can and cannot do
readme.text:
- **It cannot recover complete source code.** For native binaries upstream returns *pseudocode and
  assembly*, for Android APKs *decompiled methods*, for JEB units *pseudocode*, and for JavaScript/Electron
  *modules and their relations*. Upstream's tool contract states the pseudocode "is decompiler output, not
  original source and not text-equivalent" to another provider's output.
- Not recoverable in practice: original identifier names, types, comments, macros and template expansion,
  build scripts and assets. Optimisation (inlining, reordering), symbol stripping, obfuscation, packing and
  VM protection only make the output worse.
- Every result carries **confidence and limitations** (`observed` / `derived` / `inferred`, plus an explicit
  limitations list). Read them as evidence, never as recovered source.
- Good for: understanding behaviour, locating an implementation, interoperability and compatible
  re-implementation, security review, migration reference. To obtain actual source code, use the legitimate
  route — the upstream repository, vendor authorisation, or the vendor's own SDK.

The shipped patch uses `!!js` expressions to pick the right command at runtime:

- **Windows**: `cmd.exe /c rea --mcp` — the npm shim is a `.cmd` file, so a shell is required.
- **macOS / Linux**: `rea --mcp` — the npm shim is a direct executable on PATH.

No manual editing is needed when moving between platforms. The `--mcp` flag is the canonical stdio-server
startup form documented in `rea --help`.

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| REA (`rea-agents`) | **6.5.0** (6.3.0 or newer required) |
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.1-alpha.5` (npm CLI) |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (row provider) | `0.2.1-alpha.5`, bundled by the harness |
| Node.js | 22.19+ / 24.11+ / 26+ (REA engine requirement) |

The shipped row was exercised live: `rea --mcp` answered the MCP `initialize` handshake and returned
`serverInfo: { name: "rea", version: "6.5.0" }` with 207 tools. Every `pattern` in their input schemas
(600, 45 distinct) compiles under the Rust `regex` engine, the check strict providers such as DeepSeek's
native model apply.

- Node.js on a version REA accepts (`^22.19.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`).
- The REA CLI installed globally, **version 6.3.0 or newer**: `npm i -g rea-agents@latest`.
  Older releases advertise a tool schema with a `\0` regex escape that DeepSeek's native model rejects, so
  every turn fails while REA is connected (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)).
- For native analysis, Ghidra **12.1.x** (Hopper / IDA are alternatives under their own licences).
  Static JavaScript/Electron and .NET analysis need no engine at all.

**The plugin**

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-rea
```

Or install `dsh-rea` from the **Plugins** page in the DSH Web sidebar.

readme.section: Set up and configure — on the Plugins page
readme.text: Open **Plugins** in the DSH Web sidebar and select **REA reverse engineering**. The page has three parts:

readme.section: Set up and configure — on the Plugins page
readme.text:
1. **Setup check** — the REA CLI and its version (6.3.0+), whether the `mcp__rea__*` tools are loaded,
   Ghidra (optional), and Java (needed by Ghidra). Each item that needs attention says why and gives the
   command to fix it, with a copy button. **Check again** re-runs it.
2. **Try it** — example prompts to paste into a chat.
3. **Settings** — saved into your profile; REA restarts with the new values right away:

readme.section: Set up and configure — on the Plugins page
readme.text:
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Ghidra install directory (`ghidraInstallDir`) | empty | Passed to REA as `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`. Empty: inherit the environment variable. |
| Timeout per tool call (`toolCallTimeoutMs`) | `300000` | Decompiling a large program can take minutes. |

Without Ghidra, JavaScript / Electron and .NET analysis still work; native binaries (exe / ELF / Mach-O)
need Ghidra **12.1.x** and **JDK 21+**.

readme.section: Set up and configure — on the Plugins page
readme.text:
To pin the settings by hand instead, override the row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: rea
  config:
    ghidraInstallDir: /Applications/ghidra_12.1.1_PUBLIC
```

The setup check shows green for the REA CLI and the loaded tools. Then ask in a chat, for example
"Use REA to analyze the Electron app /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app". With Ghidra configured,
`binary_session` reports the engine checks (`configuration` / `installation` / `headless` /
`native_decompiler` / `java`), all of which should be `ok: true`.

REA exposes 207 tools at 6.5.0, so every session's tool list grows noticeably (disable the bundle on the
Plugins page when you do not need it); the row sets
`failOnStartupError: false` so a missing REA never blocks harness startup. Some REA tools launch processes,
write files and access the network — DSH's permission policy applies. Analyse only artifacts you are
authorized to inspect.

readme.section: Updating — two independent things, both manual
readme.text:
- **This plugin** never updates itself: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-rea@latest` (or the
  Plugins page). Updating REA below does **not** update this plugin, and updating this plugin does not
  touch REA.
- **Upstream REA**: `npm i -g rea-agents@latest`, then restart the harness so the MCP child respawns on the
  new binary. Its `bin` entry (`scripts/rea.mjs`) is stable across releases, so this needs no change here.
- **Ghidra** is version-gated by REA (12.1.x today): update REA first, then check that it accepts a newer
  Ghidra.
- **DeepSeek Harness**: a harness upgrade may change the MCP client's config schema — inspect the row with
  `Config.listConfigs name=@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` and adjust the field names.

**`Invalid schema for function 'mcp__rea__capture_process_scenario': "^[^=\\0]+$" is not a "regex"`**
(or any `mcp__rea__*` schema error) — the installed REA is older than 6.3.0. Its schemas use regex syntax
that DeepSeek's native model rejects, and the provider refuses the whole request. Fixed upstream in
[morluto/rea#1329](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/1329):

```
npm i -g rea-agents@latest
rea --version        # 6.3.0 or newer
```

Then restart the harness.

**No `mcp__rea__*` tools appear** — `rea` is not on the PATH the harness sees (`which rea`), or REA failed
to start; the row's `failOnStartupError: false` keeps the harness running and logs the error.

**The bundle is skipped at startup** — this release declares a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` peer range
(`0.2.x`). A harness outside it may have changed the MCP client's config schema; update this plugin.

MIT (this adapter). REA is MIT and owned by its authors; Ghidra is Apache-2.0 and owned by the NSA. No
upstream code is redistributed here.

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-rea)

把上游 **[REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea)** 的 MCP 服务接入
**DeepSeek Harness**（dsh），其工具在会话中以 `mcp__rea__*` 的形式出现。

一个小型 DSH bundle。它只有一行 `rea`：挂载官方 MCP 客户端插件（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`），
连接本机已安装的 `rea --mcp` stdio server；并在侧边栏**插件**页面提供一个页面，包含环境检查、
示例提问和设置。本包不含任何分析代码。

> **第三方适配器。** 本仓库不属于 REA，不分发任何 REA 代码，也非 REA 作者维护。它负责连接 REA 并提供设置页面。
> 上游：[github.com/morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea)（MIT）·
> [文档](https://github.com/morluto/rea#可以分析什么) ·
> [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/) · npm 包 `rea-agents`。
> REA 自身的问题去它的 tracker；**本插件的问题**去
> [本仓库 issues](https://github.com/dushudou/dsh-rea/issues)。
**它提供：** 注册 `mcp__rea__*` 工具并自动选择跨平台启动方式；在插件页面告诉你还缺什么、怎么修复。

readme.section: 能做什么 / 不能做什么
readme.text:
分析能力属于上游；本节仅复述上游自身的约定，以设定期望。

- **无法恢复完整源码。** 对原生二进制上游返回*伪代码和汇编*，Android APK 返回*反编译方法*，
  JEB 返回*伪代码*，JavaScript/Electron 返回*模块及其关系*。上游工具约定声明伪代码"是反编译器
  输出，非原始源码，且与其他提供商的输出非文本等价"。
- 实际不可恢复：原始标识符名、类型、注释、宏和模板展开、构建脚本和资源。优化（内联、重排）、
  符号剥离、混淆、加壳和虚拟机保护只会让输出更差。
- 每个结果都带有**置信度和限制说明**（`observed` / `derived` / `inferred`，加显式限制列表）。
  将它们视为证据，永远不要当作恢复的源码。
- 适用场景：理解行为、定位实现、互操作和兼容性重实现、安全审查、迁移参考。要获取实际源码，
  请走合法途径——上游仓库、厂商授权或厂商自有 SDK。

shipped patch 使用 `!!js` 表达式在运行时选择正确的命令形式：

- **Windows**：`cmd.exe /c rea --mcp` — npm shim 是 `.cmd` 文件，需要 shell。
- **macOS / Linux**：`rea --mcp` — npm shim 是 PATH 上的直接可执行文件。

跨平台无需手动编辑。`--mcp` 标志是 `rea --help` 中文档标注的 stdio server 启动方式。

| 组件 | 版本 |
|---|---|
| REA (`rea-agents`) | **6.5.0**（需要 6.3.0 或更高） |
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.1-alpha.5`（npm CLI） |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` | `0.2.1-alpha.5`，harness 自带 |
| Node.js | 22.19+ / 24.11+ / 26+（REA 引擎要求） |

shipped row 已实测：`rea --mcp` 响应了 MCP `initialize` 握手并返回
`serverInfo: { name: "rea", version: "6.5.0" }` 及 207 个工具。其输入 schema 中的全部 `pattern`
（600 个，去重后 45 个）都能被 Rust `regex` 引擎编译——DeepSeek 原生模型等严格接口做的就是这项校验。

**前置条件**

- REA 接受的 Node.js 版本（`^22.19.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`）。
- 全局安装 REA CLI，**需要 6.3.0 或更高版本**：`npm i -g rea-agents@latest`。
  更早的版本在工具 schema 里使用了 `\0` 正则转义，DeepSeek 原生模型不接受，REA 连接期间每一轮
  都会失败（见[常见问题](#常见问题)）。
- 原生分析需要 Ghidra **12.1.x**（Hopper / IDA 为替代方案，需各自授权）。
  静态 JavaScript/Electron 和 .NET 分析无需引擎。

**插件**

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-rea
```

也可以在 DSH Web 侧边栏的**插件**页面安装 `dsh-rea`。

readme.section: 设置与配置——在插件页面完成
readme.text:
打开 DSH Web 侧边栏的**插件**，选择 **REA 逆向分析**。页面分三部分：

1. **环境检查**——REA 命令行工具及版本（需 6.3.0+）、`mcp__rea__*` 工具是否已加载、Ghidra（可选）、
   Java（Ghidra 需要）。需要处理的项会说明原因并给出修复命令，可一键复制；点**重新检查**再检测一次。
2. **试一试**——可以直接贴进对话的示例提问。
3. **设置**——保存到你的 profile，REA 会立即用新设置重启：

| 设置 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| Ghidra 安装目录（`ghidraInstallDir`） | 空 | 作为 `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` 传给 REA；留空则沿用环境变量。 |
| 单次工具调用超时（`toolCallTimeoutMs`） | `300000` | 反编译大型程序可能需要几分钟。 |

readme.section: 设置与配置——在插件页面完成
readme.text:
没有 Ghidra 时，JavaScript / Electron 和 .NET 分析照常可用；原生程序（exe / ELF / Mach-O）需要
Ghidra **12.1.x** 和 **JDK 21+**。

也可以在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里手动固定设置：

```yaml
- id: rea
  config:
    ghidraInstallDir: /Applications/ghidra_12.1.1_PUBLIC
```

环境检查里 REA 命令行工具和工具加载两项显示为绿色。然后在对话里试一句，例如
"用 REA 分析 /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app 这个 Electron 应用"。配置了 Ghidra 后，
`binary_session` 会报告引擎检查（`configuration` / `installation` / `headless` /
`native_decompiler` / `java`），应全部 `ok: true`。

REA 6.5.0 暴露 207 个工具，每个会话的工具列表会明显变长（不需要时可在插件页面禁用本 bundle）；该行设置
`failOnStartupError: false`，这样 REA 缺失不会阻止 harness 启动。部分 REA 工具会启动进程、
写文件和访问网络——DSH 的权限策略会介入。只分析你有权检查的制品。

readme.section: 更新 — 两件独立的事，都是手动
readme.text:
- **本插件**不会自我更新：`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-rea@latest`（或在插件页面更新）。
  下面更新 REA **不会**更新本插件，更新本插件也不会碰 REA。
- **上游 REA**：`npm i -g rea-agents@latest`，然后重启 harness，让 MCP 子进程用新版本重新启动。
  其 `bin`（`scripts/rea.mjs`）跨版本稳定，此处无需改动。
- **Ghidra** 由 REA 版本门控（当前 12.1.x）：先更新 REA，再检查它是否接受更新的 Ghidra。
- **DeepSeek Harness**：harness 升级可能改变 MCP client 的 config schema——用
  `Config.listConfigs name=@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 检查该行并调整字段名。

**`Invalid schema for function 'mcp__rea__capture_process_scenario': "^[^=\\0]+$" is not a "regex"`**
（或任何 `mcp__rea__*` 的 schema 报错）——已安装的 REA 低于 6.3.0。它的 schema 使用了 DeepSeek
原生模型不接受的正则写法，接口会拒绝整个请求。上游已在
[morluto/rea#1329](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/1329) 修复：

```
npm i -g rea-agents@latest
rea --version        # 6.3.0 或更高
```

然后重启 harness。

**看不到 `mcp__rea__*` 工具**——harness 的 PATH 里找不到 `rea`（`which rea`），或 REA 启动失败；
该行设置了 `failOnStartupError: false`，harness 会继续运行并记录错误。

**启动时本 bundle 被跳过**——本版本声明了 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 的 peer 版本范围（`0.2.x`）。
超出该范围的 harness 可能改变了 MCP client 的配置格式，请更新本插件。

MIT（本适配器）。REA 为 MIT，版权归其作者；Ghidra 为 Apache-2.0，版权归 NSA。此处不分发任何
上游代码。
